subject: Benchmark MAP: performance deliverables & timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark MAP: performance deliverables & timeline

Hi Ben / Lena —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I want to land on a short mutual action plan (MAP) that captures the performance benchmarking deliverables we'll provide for the POC and a realistic timeline to get to an exec readout. High-level scope: latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (QPS) at target concurrencies, and a packaged export (slides + CSVs + dashboard links) for your execs.

Proposed deliverables (week-by-week):
- Week 1 (dry run): run full bench harness against a staging workload; validate measurement hooks and prefix cache behavior.
- Week 2 (formal run): capture p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, throughput at concurrency buckets (10 / 50 / 200), and record traces.
- Week 3 (packaging): assemble slides, CSV exports, and a short executive summary + dashboard snapshot.

We will share: slides (exec + deep dive), raw CSVs, dashboard links, and a one-page TL;DR for your exec review. Can you confirm the SLI targets you care about (example: TTFT p95 <= 150ms, sustained QPS target 200) and whether we should execute in your VPC or on Redwood-hosted staging?

I'll CC Marissa to own the readout slide, and Priyom will own the export artifacts.

Next step: confirm environment and PO/timeline constraints, then we’ll lock dates for the dry run (I’m proposing the week of Jun 28).

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Benchmark MAP: performance deliverables & timeline

Thanks Jonas — this looks good as a starting point. A few items from our side:

- TTFT definition: we measure time from request initiation to first token on the network (including network overhead). For our internal SLIs we use p95 <= 200ms; we’d like to see if Redwood can meet p95 <= 150ms for the smaller models.
- Concurrency mix: primary production traffic is 70% short chat messages (avg 64 tokens), 30% long-form (avg 512 tokens). We want concurrency profiles at 10/50/200 to reflect bursty RN peaks.
- Data constraints: we prefer the runs to happen in our cloud account (VPC peering) if possible — upload of masked test dataset is acceptable.

I’ve attached our perf targets doc (acme_perf_targets.docx) for reference. Also we will need a short one-page that our procurement team can attach to the PO stating deliverables and acceptance criteria.

Ben
Ben Smith
Solutions Architect, CloudApp
ben.smith@cloudapp.io

On a related note, procurement will circulate a PO template early next week.

Subject: Re: Benchmark MAP: performance deliverables & timeline

Ben — great context, thanks. Based on your SLIs and concurrency mix, here’s a concrete plan and acceptance criteria we’ll put into the MAP document:

Benchmark plan (high level):
- Measurements: latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT (p50/p95), throughput (QPS) and end-to-end service tail latency.
- Concurrency buckets: 10, 50, 200. For each bucket we'll run 1-hour sustained runs plus 5x 5-minute burst tests.
- Workloads: short (64 tokens) and long (512 tokens) mixes as you outlined.
- Environment: Redwood will run initial dry-run in our hosted staging to validate harness. Formal run will execute in your VPC via temporary peering (preferred) — we’ll send the networking checklist.

Acceptance criteria for POC sign-off:
- TTFT p95 <= 150ms for short messages (64 tokens) on the target instance family.
- Sustained QPS >= 200 across mixed workload with p95 latency under 400ms (long messages may be higher).
- Packaged deliverables: exec slide deck, deep-dive slides, CSV exports (raw time-series and aggregated metrics), Perf dashboard snapshot link.

Deliverables and artifacts (we will attach):
- redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf (slide deck / runbook)
- map_timeline_acme_v1.xlsx (detailed calendar + owners)
- ttft_qps_results.csv (raw export)
- link to live dashboard snapshot: https://redwood.app/dashboards/perf/ABC123

I’ve attached the benchmark plan (redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf) and the MAP timeline. Marissa — can you take point on assembling the exec deck once we have the CSVs? Priyom — can you own the export packaging and the CSV schema so procurement has what they need for the PO?

If this looks good I’ll author a one-page acceptance criteria doc for procurement to attach to the PO.

—Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Benchmark MAP: performance deliverables & timeline

Thanks — I’ll own the exec readout. Proposed schedule and internal owners:

- Dry run (internal validation): Jun 28 (Jonas / Priyom / Infra).
- Formal run in Acme VPC: Jul 1–2 (network checklist completed by Jun 29).
- Packaging and slide assembly: Jul 3–5 (Marissa lead, Jonas + Priyom supporting).
- Exec readout with Acme leadership: Jul 6 @ 10:00am PT (30 min + Q&A).

Slide needs: one slide with TL;DR (top-line metrics and pass/fail vs. SLIs), one slide describing environment and run parameters, two slides with p50/p95/p99 tables and CSV links, one slide with recommendations (batching/caching/quantization suggestions).

Ben / Lena: does Jul 6 10:00am PT work for your execs? I’ll draft the readout notes and a 1-page acceptance statement for procurement.

Marissa Cole

- ttft_qps_results.csv — raw request-level timings and token counts.
- map_export_package_v2.zip — includes aggregated CSVs, measurement schema README, and candidate slide images.

Notes on measurement methodology (summary):
- TTFT is measured at the agent boundary (time from POST to first byte out from model container) — this excludes customer network if we run inside your VPC; we’ll include both internal and end-to-end numbers in the final package.
- Concurrency buckets were exercised with ramp+hold loads; each bucket includes warmup + 1 hour steady-state.
- For the final package I’ll create a CSV with per-bucket aggregate rows (p50/p95/p99 TTFT and latency) and include a small script to reproduce the plots.
